title: Borders and dividers
summary: One-sided borders make dividers; border styles make a dashed drop zone.
explanation: border is shorthand for width, style and colour; the style is the part people forget, and without it nothing is drawn.
border-bottom draws a single side, which is how list dividers are made. :last-child removes the line under the final row so it does not double up with the box's own border.
Border styles go beyond solid: dashed suits a drop zone, and the 2px width with padding inside gives the dashes room.
tryThis: Remove the word solid from .row's border-bottom: the dividers disappear.
Change .drop's border style to dotted, then to double with a 4px width.
Delete the .row:last-child rule: the last row gets a line against the box border.
